spec: Rule cards for libretro cores whose save behaviour deviates from RetroArch's standard savefile_directory rule. This is world knowledge under DESIGN.md's boundary rule: each card states WHICH live config governs the core and what its values mean — the current value is always read from the machine, never from here. Cards are keyed by the core's canonical short name (the .so basename without _libretro.so, matching libretro-core-info filenames); 'identifiers' lists every name the card matches, including the display library_name the core binary reports. Facts live here; interpretation lives in code — a rule that does not fit this schema gets code plus a card referencing it, the schema does not grow a DSL. A declared file name may carry the placement's own hole tokens and nothing else (<rom_stem>, which the resolver fills from the content path, and <save_id>, which it never fills and hands to the caller as a hole); the loader refuses any other token, so a typo cannot travel into a filename atlas states as fact. The other closed vocabularies are the placement's too: 'root' and 'also_under' are savefile_directory | system_directory | content_directory (and a mode does not span its own root), 'granularity' is shared-card | per-game-file | per-game-files, and 'complete' must be a JSON boolean — never a quoted one, which Python would read as true. Format and per-field rules: atlas/data/README.md (shipped beside this file).

provenance.source: flycast_libretro.so option strings ('Per-Game VMUs', mode descriptions); live observation on RetroDECK 0.10.9b — <system_directory>/dc holds vmu_save_{A1,B1,C1,D1}.bin + dc_nvmem.bin, and a per-content run wrote <save_id>.<port>.bin for the four connected ports into the save directory the frontend handed the core. Names follow hostfs::getVmuPath (flycast@1dac369 shell/libretro/oslib.cpp:38-67): with settings.platform.isConsole() and a non-empty settings.content.gameId the name is that id — the disc's product number read from its header (core/emulator.cpp:838-841), trailing blanks trimmed, each of ' /\:*?|<>' replaced by '_' — and without one (arcade content, or a disc header stating none) the ROM's own name (oslib.cpp:62); a legacy ROM-named file is still read when no id-named one exists (oslib.cpp:55-60). The directory is RETRO_ENVIRONMENT_GET_SAVE_DIRECTORY as the frontend redirected it (shell/libretro/libretro.cpp:2142-2148), so the mode nests no subdirectory of its own. Switching modes moves the save, it does not duplicate it: the shared cards stay behind untouched. Per-content applies per port — with 'VMU A1' only port A1 moves and B1..D1 keep using the shared card (oslib.cpp:40-41), which is why that mode states no file set. dc_nvmem.bin is the console's own flash, shared by every game in every mode, and stays under <system_directory>/dc throughout. Slot-2 VMUs (A2..D2) exist only when a port's slot 2 is configured as VMU; on Naomi the connected VMUs are B1 and C1 (core/hw/maple/maple_cfg.cpp:246-253).

provenance.source: opera-libretro source: opera_lr_nvram.c:117-175 — NVRAM is written to '<save_dir>/opera/per_game/<rom_stem>.<version>.srm' (per game) or '<save_dir>/opera/shared/nvram.<version>.srm' (shared); <version> comes from opera_nvram_version (values 0-7, default 0, libretro_core_options.c:286-301), which is why per-mode file lists are omitted rather than declared. save_dir falls back to system_dir only when the frontend provides none (opera_lr_nvram.c:102-113) — never the case under RetroArch. RETRO_MEMORY_SAVE_RAM returns NULL (libretro.c:574-579), so these files are the ONLY persistence; no RetroArch-side .srm exists. Legacy locations are tried at load only: '<save_dir>/<rom_stem>.srm', '<system_dir>/<rom_stem>.srm', '<save_dir|system_dir>/3DO.nvram' (opera_lr_nvram.c:177-349). The shipped RetroDECK 0.10.9b binary carries the same option keys and path constants (unfiltered strings check).
